```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# We only need the core 'glue' package for HTML assembly
if(!requireNamespace("glue", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("glue", repos = "[https://cloud.r-project.org](https://cloud.r-project.org)")
}
library(glue)

cal_id <- "c_6eluv1h8o830k7vt8ctcs6ghto@group.calendar.google.com"
url <- paste0("[https://calendar.google.com/calendar/ical/](https://calendar.google.com/calendar/ical/)", URLencode(cal_id), "/public/basic.ics")

tryCatch({
  tmp_ics <- tempfile(fileext = ".ics")
  
  # Cross-platform download engine
  if (Sys.info()[["sysname"]] == "Windows") {
    download.file(url, destfile = tmp_ics, method = "wininet", quiet = TRUE)
  } else {
    download.file(url, destfile = tmp_ics, method = "wget", quiet = TRUE)
  }
  
  lines <- readLines(tmp_ics, warn = FALSE)
  
  # Parse individual VEVENT blocks from the raw iCal text
  event_starts <- which(lines == "BEGIN:VEVENT")
  event_ends   <- which(lines == "END:VEVENT")
  
  events_list <- list()
  
  if (length(event_starts) > 0) {
    for (i in seq_along(event_starts)) {
      ev_lines <- lines[event_starts[i]:event_ends[i]]
      
      # Extract key attributes out of the raw text strings
      summary_line <- ev_lines[grep("^SUMMARY:", ev_lines)]
      dtstart_line <- ev_lines[grep("^DTSTART([;:])", ev_lines)]
      
      if (length(summary_line) > 0 && length(dtstart_line) > 0) {
        summary_text <- sub("^SUMMARY:", "", summary_line)
        
        # Pull out raw timestamp strings (e.g., "20261024T180000Z")
        raw_time <- sub("^DTSTART.*:", "", dtstart_line)
        
        # Parse timestamp into a formal R time object
        clean_time <- tryCatch({
          if (grepl("Z$", raw_time)) {
            as.POSIXct(raw_time, format="%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ", tz="UTC")
          } else {
            as.POSIXct(sub("T.*", "", raw_time), format="%Y%m%d", tz="America/New_York")
          }
        }, error = function(e) NULL)
        
        if (!is.null(clean_time)) {
          events_list[[length(events_list) + 1]] <- list(
            summary = summary_text,
            start = clean_time
          )
        }
      }
    }
  }
  
  # Filter out events in the past and grab the nearest future entry
  current_time <- Sys.time()
  future_events <- Filter(function(x) x$start >= current_time, events_list)
  
  if (length(future_events) > 0) {
    # Sort events chronologically
    future_events <- future_events[order(sapply(future_events, function(x) x$start))]
    next_event <- future_events[[1]]
    
    # Format dates/times beautifully in Eastern Time
    date_est  <- format(next_event$start, "%B %d, %Y", tz="America/New_York")
    time_est  <- format(next_event$start, "%H:%M %Z", tz="America/New_York")
    summary_txt <- next_event$summary
    
    # Render the compact HTML directly without nested code blocks
    html_output <- paste0(
      '<div class="fims-meeting-card">',
        '<div class="fims-meeting-content">',
          '<h3 class="no-anchor">Next Meeting</h3>',
          '<p class="mb-4 opacity-75">', summary_txt, '</p>',
          '<div class="fims-meeting-datetime">',
            '<div class="fims-meeting-row">',
              '<i class="bi bi-calendar-event-fill fims-icon-danger"></i> <strong>', date_est, '</strong>',
            '</div>',
            '<div class="fims-meeting-row">',
              '<i class="bi bi-clock-fill fims-icon-danger"></i> <strong>', time_est, '</strong>',
            '</div>',
          '</div>',
        '</div>',
        '<a href="[https://calendar.google.com/calendar/u/0?cid=Y182ZWx1djFoOG84MzBrN3Z0OGN0Y3M2Z2h0b0Bncm91cC5jYWxlbmRhci5nb29nbGUuY29t](https://calendar.google.com/calendar/u/0?cid=Y182ZWx1djFoOG84MzBrN3Z0OGN0Y3M2Z2h0b0Bncm91cC5jYWxlbmRhci5nb29nbGUuY29t)" target="_blank" class="btn btn-light fims-btn-full">Add to calendar</a>',
      '</div>'
    )
    cat(html_output)
    
  } else {
    stop("No future events found")
  }
  
}, error = function(e) {
  # Universal fallback card if no meetings are returned or network glitches
  fallback_output <- paste0(
    '<div class="fims-meeting-card">',
      '<div class="fims-meeting-content">',
        '<h3 class="no-anchor">Next Meeting</h3>',
        '<p class="mb-4 opacity-75">No upcoming meetings scheduled.</p>',
      '</div>',
    '</div>'
  )
  cat(fallback_output)
})
```

::: {.fims-contribute-header}
## Ways to Contribute
Whether you're a seasoned modeler or a first-time open-source contributor, there's a place for you in the FIMS community.
:::

::: {.fims-card-grid}
::: {.fims-card}
::: {.fims-card-icon}
<i class="bi bi-terminal-fill"></i>
:::
### Code & Logic
Help implement new population dynamics features or optimize existing C++ and R libraries.

* <i class="bi bi-check-circle-fill fims-text-success"></i> Good first issues
* <i class="bi bi-check-circle-fill fims-text-success"></i> Bug triaging
:::

::: {.fims-card}
::: {.fims-card-icon}
<i class="bi bi-file-earmark-text-fill"></i>
:::
### Documentation
Clarify scientific methods, write tutorials, or improve our API documentation and guides.

* <i class="bi bi-check-circle-fill fims-text-success"></i> Wiki updates
* <i class="bi bi-check-circle-fill fims-text-success"></i> Use-case studies
:::

::: {.fims-card}
::: {.fims-card-icon}
<i class="bi bi-diagram-3-fill"></i>
:::
### Scientific Peer Review
Participate in working groups to validate the mathematical integrity of new modeling modules.

* <i class="bi bi-check-circle-fill fims-text-success"></i> Technical review
* <i class="bi bi-check-circle-fill fims-text-success"></i> Algorithm testing
:::
:::

::: {.fims-steps-section}
::: {.fims-steps-intro}
## Getting Involved
Follow these 4 simple steps to start contributing to the FIMS project today.

![](../images/fims_dashboard.png){.fims-steps-img}
:::

::: {.fims-steps-list}
::: {.fims-step}
::: {.fims-step-number}
1
:::
::: {.fims-step-content}
#### Introduce Yourself
Introduce yourself on the FIMS discussion board and start following discussions and the FIMS repository.

<a href="https://github.com/orgs/NOAA-FIMS/discussions/801" class="fims-step-link">Introduce Yourself <i class="bi bi-box-arrow-up-right"></i></a>
:::
:::

::: {.fims-step}
::: {.fims-step-number}
2
:::
::: {.fims-step-content}
#### Go through the FIMS Vignettes
Go through the FIMS vignettes to understand the package's functionality.

<a href="https://noaa-fims.github.io/FIMS/" class="fims-step-link">Learn Now <i class="bi bi-file-text"></i></a>
:::
:::

::: {.fims-step}
::: {.fims-step-number}
3
:::
::: {.fims-step-content}
#### Review Contribution Guide
Read our technical standards for contributing to FIMS.

<a href="https://github.com/NOAA-FIMS/FIMS/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md" class="fims-step-link">Read Guide <i class="bi bi-file-text"></i></a>
:::
:::

::: {.fims-step}
::: {.fims-step-number}
4
:::
::: {.fims-step-content}
#### Come to Code Club and other FIMS trainings
Attend FIMS Code Clubs and trainings to learn more about contributing to FIMS and connect with other contributors. You don't need to be an expert to attend - these are meant to be welcoming spaces for learning and collaboration!

<a href="../about/calendar.html'" class="fims-step-link">Browse Calendar <i class="bi bi-people"></i></a>
:::
:::

::: {.fims-step}
::: {.fims-step-number}
5
:::
::: {.fims-step-content}
#### Start Small
Pick a 'Good First Issue' on GitHub and submit your first pull request for peer review.

<a href="https://github.com/NOAA-FIMS/FIMS/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22good%20first%20issue%22" class="btn btn-dark fims-btn-small">Find First Issue</a>
:::
:::
:::
:::
